mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking starch into shorter chains and then glucose was most worthwhile: the two steps made it clear how a large food molecule becomes small enough to cross the intestinal lining.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the three organs was straightforward but repetitive because each had a named slot.

surprise.text: Bile disperses fat into droplets, while lipase breaks the fat apart; bile itself is not an enzyme. Monoglycerides were named but not explained further.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the organ fittings mostly involved following named slots rather than deciding how digestion works.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, to see how the glucose, amino acids and fat digestion products actually cross the gut lining and reach the body.
